Nandini: he came to my building again tonight
Sunaina: what? did he go up?
Nandini: security stopped him at the gate. he kept saying he only wanted to talk
Nandini: 14 calls today and messages since morning
Sunaina: have you answered any of them?
Nandini: I sent one last week. "It's over. Please don't contact me again." nothing since
Sunaina: good. don't reply to anything now
Nandini: I'm saving every screenshot and the call log
Sunaina: tell your parents tonight, and if he turns up again go to the police with the screenshots
Nandini: I'll tell Papa now
Sunaina: I'm coming over

qa.q: Who stopped Nandini's ex at the gate?
qa.a: Security stopped him at the gate.

qa.q: What does Nandini's saving of screenshots and the call log suggest Nandini is worried about?
qa.a: That the contact may continue or get worse, so a record will be needed for trusted people or the police.

qa.q: What has Nandini already done well, and what should follow?
qa.a: Nandini sent one clear final message and stopped replying; next come keeping records, telling family tonight and going to the police if he appears again.

qa.q: How does Sunaina react to the news?
qa.a: Sunaina is concerned and comes over at once.

grounding: An ex keeps calling and turning up after a clear no; the protagonist keeps one boundary, stops engaging, keeps records and tells trusted people.

passage:
Monday, the first week. Binita had ended it with Anirban on Saturday. By Monday he had sent forty messages: "Just talk to me." "You owe me that." She replied to some, trying to be kind. Each reply brought ten more. She felt uneasy, checking her phone every few minutes.

The following Monday. Binita wrote one message, read it to her friend Shreya first, and sent it: "Anirban, it's over. Please don't contact me again. I won't be replying." Then she blocked him, saved screenshots of every message with dates, and told her flatmates, her parents and her team lead at work.

Two weeks later. Anirban was waiting outside her office gate at six. Binita's heart pounded. She didn't stop or speak. She went back inside and told the security guard, who walked her to her cab. That evening, with her father beside her, she took her screenshots to the police station and filed a complaint. The officer took it seriously.

qa.q: How many messages had Anirban sent by Monday?
How did Binita feel as the messages kept coming?
qa.a: Binita felt uneasy and on edge, checking her phone every few minutes.

qa.q: What steps did Binita take to protect herself?
qa.a: She sent one clear final message, stopped engaging, blocked him, kept dated records, told trusted people, and went to the police when he turned up.
Shreya listened to Binita's final message before she sent it, helping her feel supported in setting the boundary.

grounding: The story shows a young woman whose ex keeps contacting her and turns up after she ended it, who sets one clear boundary, stops engaging, keeps records, tells trusted people and goes to the police.

passage:
Madhav, you think only girls get followed around by an ex? Let your Vikas mama tell you what happened to me at twenty-four.

When I ended things with Rhea, she didn't accept it. First it was calls, thirty a day. Then she started turning up at my office canteen. Then outside my rented room at night, knocking.

I felt uneasy all the time, and embarrassed. Who would believe a man was scared?

My turning point was my elder brother. He said, "Being scared is not weakness. Stop answering her. Say it once, clearly, and then write everything down."

So I sent one message: "Rhea, it's over. Please do not contact me or come here again." After that, nothing. I noted every call and visit in a diary with dates. I told my landlord, my manager and my brother.

When she came at midnight a week later, my brother came with me to the police station the next morning. They spoke to her family. It stopped.

qa.q: How many calls a day did Rhea make at first?
qa.a: She made thirty calls a day.

qa.q: How did young Vikas feel while Rhea kept turning up?
qa.a: He felt uneasy all the time and embarrassed, worried nobody would believe a man could be scared.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Vikas's story?
qa.a: His brother told him being scared wasn't weakness, so he gave one clear final message, stopped responding, kept records, told trusted people and went to the police.

qa.q: How did Vikas's brother see the situation?
qa.a: His brother took it seriously as a safety problem and stayed by Vikas's side through the steps.

grounding: An elder's story shows a young man whose ex kept calling and turning up after he ended it, who gave one clear final boundary, stopped engaging, kept records, told trusted people and went to the police.
